mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < previous 6-month average) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 6-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO < 98 for three consecutive months) indicates supply-side stress, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower corporate earnings and input cost pressures.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during INDPRO < 98 for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 3.0% coupled with a concurrent rise in real savings (RSAFS YoY growth > 4%) signals a liquidity trap environment, which historically supports equity valuations via lower borrowing costs and increased cash seeking yield, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during triggered liquidity trap episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) alongside a simultaneous acceleration in housing starts (HOUST > previous month by > 5%) signals strengthening household demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days via higher consumption and construction spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% AND HOUST > previous month by > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during triggered early-cycle episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and margin compression.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > 4.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three-month stretches of CPI > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher consumer spending and wage growth boosting corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during UNRATE < 3.5% for four months.
